# AAIA Summer Intensive 2026 Workshop — Medium App Clone

This repository is the shared starting point for the AAIA Summer Intensive 2026
development workshop. It is a working **Medium clone ("Conduit")** built with
**Django + HTMX** — a real application with real complexity: authentication,
articles, comments, tags, favorites, following, and feeds.

It is cloned from the upstream open-source project
[c4ffein/realworld-django-htmx](https://github.com/c4ffein/realworld-django-htmx)
and prepared so that everyone in the workshop builds from the **same
application**. The upstream project pulls its CSS, icons, and end-to-end test
suite from a Git submodule; we have **inlined all of that directly into the
repository** — so there is no submodule step. You clone, install, and run.

## Getting started

The only prerequisite is [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (which manages Python
and all dependencies for you).

```shell
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone <your-assigned-repo-url>
cd <repo-directory>

# 2. Install dependencies (Python + packages)
uv sync --extra dev

# 3. Set up the database
DEBUG=True uv run python manage.py migrate

# 4. Start the app
DEBUG=True uv run python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000
```

Then open **http://localhost:8000** — you should see the Conduit home page,
fully styled. Register an account from the **Sign up** link and start using the
app.

---

> ### Django + HTMX codebase containing real world examples (CRUD, auth, advanced patterns, etc) that adheres to the [RealWorld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld) spec.

### [RealWorld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld)

A fullstack [RealWorld](https://github.com/realworld-apps/realworld) implementation (Medium clone) using **Django** for server-rendered HTML and **HTMX** for interactive elements — no API, no SPA.

#### Architecture

Helper `user.is_following(other)` checks `other.followers.filter(pk=user.id).exists()`. For blocking you'd add another `symmetrical=False` self-M2M, e.g. `blocked = models.ManyToManyField("self", symmetrical=False, related_name="blocked_by", blank=True)` with a helper like `is_blocking(other)` / `is_blocked_by(other)`. ### View File: `/home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-0/apps/accounts/views.py`, `follow_view` (lines 129–151). """Unit tests for the user-blocking relationship helpers.

Broader behaviour (buttons, guards, management page) is covered by the
Playwright e2e suite; these tests pin the model-level semantics that are
awkward to observe through the browser.
"""

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import TestCase

User = get_user_model()


class BlockingModelTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = User.objects.create_user(email="alice@example.com", username="alice", password="pw")
        self.bob = User.objects.create_user(email="bob@example.com", username="bob", password="pw")

    def test_has_blocked_is_directional(self):
        self.alice.blocked.add(self.bob)
        self.assertTrue(self.alice.has_blocked(self.bob))
        self.assertFalse(self.bob.has_blocked(self.alice))

    def test_is_blocked_by_reverse(self):
        self.alice.blocked.add(self.bob)
        self.assertTrue(self.bob.is_blocked_by(self.alice))
        self.assertFalse(self.alice.is_blocked_by(self.bob))

    def test_can_interact_with_is_mutual(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.alice.can_interact_with(self.bob))
        self.alice.blocked.add(self.bob)
        # neither direction can interact once a block exists
        self.assertFalse(self.alice.can_interact_with(self.bob))
        self.assertFalse(self.bob.can_interact_with(self.alice))

## Summary

I added **user blocking** to the Django + HTMX RealWorld app, mirroring the existing follow feature's patterns.

### How it works
- **Model** (`apps/accounts/models.py`): a new self-referential `blocked` M2M on `User` (symmetric to how `followers` works), plus helpers `has_blocked()`, `is_blocked_by()`, and `can_interact_with()` (true only when neither user has blocked the other). Migration `0004_user_blocked.py`.
- **Blocking a user**: a **Block/Unblock** button on every other user's profile (`partials/profile_actions.html`), toggled via HTMX like the follow button. Blocking also severs any existing follow relationship in both directions.
- **Preventing interaction** — once A blocks B (enforced server-side, the real protection):
  - `follow_view` refuses to follow when a block exists either way, and the Follow button is hidden.
  - `comment_create_view` returns `403` and the comment form is hidden on the article page.
  - `article_favorite_view` returns `403`.
- **Managing blocks**: a **"Manage blocked users"** page (`/blocked`, linked from Settings) lists everyone you've blocked with an **Unblock** button each.

### Verification
- `make verify` — lint, type-check, unit tests: **pass** (added `apps/accounts/tests.py` covering the model semantics; the pre-existing `ty` warnings are baseline and non-blocking).
- `make e2e` — **78 passed, 65 skipped, 0 failed**, including 4 new blocking specs (`realworld/specs/e2e/blocking.spec.ts`): block/unblock toggle, blocked-user-can't-follow, blocked-user-can't-comment, and managing blocks from settings. No regressions to the existing suite.

Two notes for you:
- I added `node_modules/` and the Playwright report/results dirs to `.gitignore` (they were generated by running the e2e suite and weren't previously ignored). I had to `bun install` since `node_modules/` wasn't present in the checkout.
- The blocking tests live in the shared `realworld/specs/e2e/` dir but are guarded with `test.skip(API_MODE)` since blocking is a fullstack-only feature, not part of the RealWorld API spec.

The implementation is left in the working tree; no PR opened.
